summary: The note describes a series of mental health wellness workshops offered by local health organizations starting September 15, 2023. It explains the benefits of attending, how to choose a workshop, the types available, what to expect, and the role of support systems. It also lists upcoming October and November events and stresses continuing self-care after the workshops.
one_line: Overview of local mental health wellness workshops starting September 15, 2023, covering benefits, selection tips, workshop types, upcoming events and long-term support.
key_facts: A series of interactive wellness workshops on mental health management began on September 15, 2023, run by local health organizations.
Dr. Elaine Richardson, a renowned psychologist, will helm the upcoming workshop series and says the sessions can be life-changing.

John Avery, a mental health advocate and frequent workshop facilitator, says: "Workshops are about learning and growth, but also about finding your tribe – those who get your journey and can walk alongside you."
Tips for choosing a workshop: gauge your comfort level, identify your goals, consider the facilitators' expertise, and review the curriculum.
Workshop types include Stress and Anxiety, Mindfulness and Meditation, Emotional Intelligence, and Wellness and Lifestyle workshops.
Mindfulness and meditation workshops are often overseen by mindfulness coach Lisa Chang.
Wellness and Lifestyle workshops are directed by holistic health coaches like Michael Thompson and cover nutrition, exercise and sleep.
Workshops may include lectures, discussions, group activities such as role-playing, and sometimes one-on-one or individual counseling sessions.
Special sessions may educate friends, family and employers on how to support someone with mental health challenges, in order to break the stigma.
October sessions focus on mental health and technology, led by cyber wellness expert David Miller.
A November workshop on "Resilience Training" will feature guest speaker Maya Jenkins and cover developing mental toughness.
Attendees are commonly provided with resources and follow-up support so they do not walk the road to better mental health alone.
